filter.order_actual_note: scipy.signal.butter(4, ..., btype='band') returns an order-2N=8 bandpass filter; sosfiltfilt applies it forward and backward, squaring the magnitude response again. The nominal 'order 4' describes the design request, not the realized filter order.
filter.notch_form_note: iirnotch only produces the (b, a) form. Rule 4's sos requirement targets the 0.5 Hz highpass edge (normalized frequency 0.0039), where (b, a) is numerically unstable; at 60 Hz / 256 Hz the normalized frequency is 0.469 and (b, a) is well conditioned.
filter.filtered_one_channel_at_a_time: Each channel is read and filtered over its full length independently, then all of its windows are extracted, before the next channel is read. This is a memory layout change only - the filter still sees the entire recording, never a single window (rule 3).
filter.realtime_limitation: filtfilt (both bandpass and notch) is zero-phase and non-causal - it uses future samples. Not usable in a real-time/streaming device; a real device would need a causal one-directional IIR filter, which introduces phase distortion affecting detection latency. Record this in the paper's Limitations section.

windowing.label_rule: window labeled 1 if overlap with a seizure interval >= 50% of window duration
windowing.label_rule_locked_level: 3 - arbitrary choice, requires sensitivity analysis in spec 2

deviation.what: Windows are taken on a uniform 4 s grid (contiguous, non-overlapping, 100% temporal coverage) instead of the locked 0.5 s step, plus a 0.5 s dense schedule inside seizure_start - 60 s to seizure_end + 60 s. Every row carries on_uniform_grid; the dense rows exist only to give training folds enough positive windows and are excluded from every evaluation.
deviation.why: The chosen schedule is 907,755 windows and took 13.34 h wall (measured, 12 workers on a 6P+8E core laptop, 666 files, 0 failures) for 9.1 GB of feature parquet. The locked 0.5 s step over the same Tier A base is 6,802,824 windows - 7.5x more - which extrapolates to ~100 h and 62.6 GB, against ceilings of 12 h and 20 GB in CLAUDE.md section 11. A 4 s grid with a 4 s window is the coarsest schedule that still covers 100% of the recordings, which is what keeps recorded hours a valid denominator for false alarms per day (rule 5.2).

measured_runtime.note: Throughput was strongly bimodal: ~8.5 windows/s over the 86 recordings longer than 2.5 h and ~32 windows/s over the 552 recordings of about 1 h. The cause is I/O, not compute. To keep memory bounded, each recording is read one channel at a time, so a file is read 21 times; 12 workers on 4-hour files hold ~7.2 GB of EDF against a 15.7 GB machine and every re-read reaches the disk, while 1-hour files stay in the page cache. Anyone re-estimating this pipeline must weight by file duration - a probe on a 1-hour file underestimates the long recordings by about 4x.

deviation.runtime_estimate_history: Two earlier estimates for this schedule were wrong and must not be quoted. ~14 h projected wall time from the single-core cost (19.1 ms per channel per window) scaled by a 7.4x parallel speedup measured on the entropy kernel in isolation, which the full pipeline does not reach. ~29.6 h extrapolated from the first 12 completed files, which were the longest recordings in the study and the slowest per window by 4x. The measured figure is 13.34 h.
deviation.evaluation_rule: All sensitivity / false-alarm figures are computed on on_uniform_grid == True rows only, so the evaluation timeline is uniform and no region of the recording is over-represented. Training may use every row.
deviation.cost: Post-processing at grid resolution is quantized to 4 s. The shortest seizure in the Tier A base is 6 s and every one of the 181 seizures gets at least 2 grid windows labelled positive (median 12), so a 'k consecutive positive windows' rule is capped at k=1 before short seizures become undetectable by construction (CLAUDE.md section 12). Finer post-processing sweeps are possible only inside the dense zone and must be reported as a secondary analysis.
deviation.who_approved: Project owner, 2026-08-14, in an interactive session with Claude Code.

band_note: Project-locked bands (delta 1-4, theta 4-8, alpha 8-13, beta 13-30) are used in place of DIHC_FeatureManager's own defaults (delta 0-5, theta 5-8, alpha 8-14, beta 14-31) because the library defaults touch the filter's transition/stop bands (e.g. delta starting at 0 Hz is inside our 0.5 Hz highpass stopband). 'other' stands in for DIHC's gamma band and intentionally spans beyond our 40 Hz passband (30-128 Hz) - see feature docstring.

dropped_duplicates_at_load_time.P7-T7: polarity-flipped copy of T7-P7 (signal = -1 x original)
dropped_duplicates_at_load_time.T8-P8 (second occurrence): byte-identical duplicate of the first T8-P8; recorder configuration error

channels.missing_channel_policy: A required derivation absent from a file yields NaN for all of that channel's feature columns in that file - never 0 (CLAUDE.md section 9). Counts are reported in 01_dataset_summary.md.

features.dihc_library_source: https://github.com/WWM-EMRAN/DIHC_FeatureManager (no PyPI package; reverse-engineered from source, no official version tag)
features.azc_source: Zanetti et al. 2022 (J. Neural Eng.) - own reimplementation, no reference code found. Method: raw zero-crossing count, plus Douglas-Peucker polygonal approximation (vertical/amplitude distance criterion) at thresholds 16/32/64/128/256 uV, each followed by a zero-crossing count on the approximated signal.
features.feature_selection: NONE in the feature parquet - raw features only. chi-squared selection (top-30 per channel) is fit inside each CV fold by train.py (spec 2 / docs/06, written and run).
features.scaling_normalization: NONE in the feature parquet - MinMaxScaler is fit inside each CV fold by train.py (spec 2 / docs/06, written and run).

feature_scope_deviation.what: The 9 entropyProfiled_* features (entropyProfiled_total/average/maximum/minimum/median/standardDeviation/variance/kurtosis/skewness_sampleEntropy) are dropped from the 92-feature DIHC_FeatureManager-equivalent library. 83 of 92 DIHC features + all 6 AZC features are extracted (89 features x 21 channels = 1869 feature columns).
feature_scope_deviation.why: Benchmarked on real EEG (not synthetic data): the entropy-profile computation costs ~496 ms per channel per window, against 19.1 ms for all 89 retained features combined. It would roughly triple the extraction cost even after the same kind of rewrite the other O(N^2) entropies received, and would add a second bespoke kernel to audit for fidelity to the upstream source.
feature_scope_deviation.correction_to_earlier_record: The 2026-08-12 version of this entry justified the drop with '~68 days for all 92 features' and '~1 ms for the other 83 features combined', and predicted ~2.4 days for the 83. Both were wrong: the 83 features measured 100.3 ms per channel per window, and the run they predicted at 2.4 days was on track for ~17.5 days when it was killed. The decision stands on the corrected numbers above; the superseded figures must not be quoted in the paper.
feature_scope_deviation.rebenchmark_2026_08_19: entropyProfiled re-benchmarked on real data at ~1.4-1.5 s per channel per window - about 3x the ~496 ms above, which is also a superseded estimate. Extracting the 9 entropyProfiled_* features for the whole dataset (18,984,141 channel-windows) would take ~259 days at the measured pilot rate (1.178 s/channel-window). Keeping only entropyProfiled_total saves nothing: sample_entropy_profile() must be computed in full before any summary statistic. Full-dataset extraction is infeasible and will not be run.
feature_scope_deviation.pilot_result_2026_08_19: chi-squared pilot (2000 stratified windows, 13 subjects, 79 files; output/00f_entropy_pilot.md): entropyProfiled_total_sampleEntropy places in the chi-squared top-30 in all 21 of 21 scoreable channels (best feature in most). So the exclusion is NOT a harmless cost-only deviation - it must be written as a real limitation in Methods. A lightweight impact test (output/00f_entropy_pilot_impact_test.md; Full-18, GroupKFold(5), window-level AUC-ROC only) found adding entropyProfiled_total changes pooled AUC by +0.0010 (0.6629 -> 0.6638), i.e. the univariate chi-squared signal does not translate into a measurable cross-subject generalisation gain in that small test. Limitation is two-layer: (1) dropped for cost, not for lack of value; (2) preliminary evidence that it may not help generalisation much.
feature_scope_deviation.who_approved: Project owner, 2026-08-12; re-confirmed 2026-08-14 after the numbers were corrected; not-run-on-full-dataset decision confirmed jointly 2026-08-19.
feature_scope_deviation.deviates_from: The preprocessing spec's 'extract all 92, no selection at this stage'.

performance_optimization.what: features.py was rewritten for speed: 100.3 -> 19.1 ms per channel per window (5.3x), measured on real CHB-MIT data on a single core. Three changes account for almost all of it: (a) approximateEntropy, fuzzyEntropy and distributionEntropy now share one pass over the pairwise Chebyshev distances of the delay embedding instead of three separate scipy pdist calls (63.5 -> 17.0 ms); (b) the AZC Douglas-Peucker approximation is numba-compiled (19.3 -> 0.11 ms); (c) the frequency-domain block computes moments directly instead of through scipy.stats and reuses its Welch PSD for spectral entropy (16.4 -> 4.5 ms).
performance_optimization.verification: The pre-optimization implementation is frozen verbatim in src/features_reference.py and src/validate_features.py recomputes all 89 features both ways on 252 real filtered CHB-MIT windows spanning 3 subjects, ictal and interictal. Result: 86 of 89 features bit-identical; the other 3 (fuzzyEntropy, approximateEntropy, fd_kurtosis) agree to a largest relative difference of 6.7e-14, i.e. floating-point accumulation order only. See output/00c_feature_parity.md.
performance_optimization.parallel_scaling_caveat: The 19.1 ms figure is single-core and unloaded. Running 12 workers, each costs ~68 ms per channel per window, so aggregate throughput is ~3.4x a single core rather than ~12x. The fused kernel materialises a 4 MB distance buffer per window for distributionEntropy's histogram; 12 of those exceed the machine's 24 MB shared L3. Anyone reporting per-window cost must say which of the two numbers they mean.

known_degenerate_or_redundant_features.issue: DIHC_FeatureManager only computes real sample entropy for len(window) >= 5000 samples (antropy.sample_entropy is O(N^2) and the source guards against it). Our windows are 1024 samples (4s @ 256Hz), so this feature is identically 0.0 for every window.
known_degenerate_or_redundant_features.action: Kept as 0.0 (faithful to source), not removed.

known_degenerate_or_redundant_features.issue: Source computes len(scipy.signal.find_peaks(x)) / len(scipy.signal.find_peaks(-x)). find_peaks() returns a 2-tuple (indices, properties); len() of that tuple is always 2 regardless of input, so this feature is identically 1.0 for every window. Almost certainly an upstream bug (missing [0] indexing into the peak-index array).
known_degenerate_or_redundant_features.action: Reproduced faithfully. Emitted as the constant 1.0 it provably is, rather than by calling find_peaks twice per window to rediscover it; verified identical in 00c_feature_parity.md.

known_degenerate_or_redundant_features.issue: antropy.lziv_complexity casts float input to uint32 without binarizing first (documented antropy behaviour, not a bug in antropy - the caller is expected to binarize). DIHC calls it directly on continuous uV amplitudes; negative values wrap around under the uint32 cast. The result is deterministic given the input but does not measure the intended complexity notion.
known_degenerate_or_redundant_features.action: Reproduced faithfully (ant.lziv_complexity(x) on raw amplitudes), not fixed.

known_degenerate_or_redundant_features.issue: Computed via collections.Counter on raw continuous amplitude values (source code), which are almost all unique per window -> the resulting distribution is close to uniform over N samples regardless of signal content, so this feature is close to a constant log2(N) = log2(1024) = 10 for nearly every window.

DIHC wraps pyeeg.fisher_info. pyeeg's source for fisher_info is -sum(W*log(W)) on the normalized SVD spectrum of the delay embedding (tau=1, m=2) - mathematically identical to pyeeg's own svd_entropy formula. Expected to be highly correlated with singularValueDecompositionEntropy (which uses antropy's svd_entropy, same mathematical form, possibly different order/delay defaults).
known_degenerate_or_redundant_features.action: Reproduced the literal pyeeg formula faithfully. Flag for possible redundancy in feature selection results.

known_degenerate_or_redundant_features.issue: This project's bandpass filter is 0.5-40 Hz. The 'other' band (30-128 Hz, standing in for DIHC's own default gamma band of 31-100 Hz) sits almost entirely outside the filter passband, so these 9 features are expected to be near-zero by construction, not by signal content. Anticipated by CLAUDE.md section 7.
known_degenerate_or_redundant_features.action: Kept (not removed) per CLAUDE.md instruction; report near-zero values.

subjects.merge_reason: chb21 is the same patient as chb01, recorded ~1.5 years later (Ali et al. 2024 note this but do not merge). Merging prevents patient leakage across LOSO folds.

selection_deviation.what: Files are admitted individually (Tier A) instead of admitting only subjects whose every file carries all 21 derivations. Tier A = all 18 double-banana derivations present and the file is not one of chb12's three monopolar recordings. Configurations that need T7-FT9/FT9-FT10/FT10-T8 (only Glass-7) are evaluated on the Tier B subset of those files; every other configuration uses the full Tier A base.
selection_deviation.why: The previous rule - impose the Glass-7 channel requirement on every configuration so that all configurations share one subject base (CLAUDE.md section 8) - excluded 7 of 23 subjects and 81 of 181 seizures (45%). CLAUDE.md section 11 requires stopping and asking above 3 excluded subjects. The cost of the change is that Glass-7 is reported against a slightly smaller base (640 files / 177 seizures) than the other configurations (668 files / 181 seizures); this must be stated wherever the two are compared, and the Best-n vs Glass-n curves that carry the study's argument all sit on the identical 181-seizure base.
selection_deviation.who_approved: Project owner, 2026-08-14, in an interactive session with Claude Code.
selection_deviation.deviates_from: CLAUDE.md section 8: 'every configuration should be evaluated on the same subject base'.

glass7_vs_best7.what: The Best-7 vs Glass-7 comparison is the weakest rung of the channel ladder, and both sources of unfairness lean in Glass-7's favour. It must not carry the study's headline claim about the cost of the eyeglass position constraint; that claim rests on Best-4 vs Glass-4 and Best-2 vs Glass-2, which share both the candidate pool and the 181-seizure Tier A base.
glass7_vs_best7.problem_1_candidate_pool: Best-7 is selected from the 18 double-banana channels, which do NOT contain T7-FT9 / FT9-FT10 / FT10-T8 - three of Glass-7's seven channels. This is not 'free choice vs a constrained subset of the same universe', it is two partly disjoint universes. 'Best-7' here means 'best 7 of a standard double-banana montage', not 'best possible 7'; selection allowed the full 21 unique derivations could do better. Consequence: if Glass-7 matches or beats Best-7 (finding B1 in Consolidated-Context.md, seen intermittently), that does not cleanly show the position constraint is free, because Best-7 was not allowed the full pool either. Rationale for the restriction: the FT9-chain channels ARE the glasses-frame derivations, so putting them in Best-7's pool would let Best-7 pick the glasses channels and blur the unconstrained-vs-constrained contrast rather than sharpen it - a defensible trade-off, but one to state plainly.
glass7_vs_best7.problem_2_evaluation_base: Glass-7 is scored on Tier B (640 files / 917.48 h / 177 seizures); Best-7 on Tier A (668 / 945.49 / 181). No subject is dropped - 23 in both tiers - but the files Tier B loses are concentrated in hard cases: the 4 missing seizures (181 -> 177) are all from chb13 (12 -> 10) and chb16 (10 -> 8), the two shortest-seizure subjects in the dataset (chb16 holds the 6 s minimum; chb13 is a mechanism-1 short/sparse case, Consolidated-Context.md B3). Glass-7 is therefore evaluated on a marginally easier base than Best-7 - about 2.2% of seizures, and the hardest 2.2%.
glass7_vs_best7.how_to_report: Always state Glass-7's base (177 seizures / 917.48 h) next to any number compared with a Tier A config. Define Best-7 in Methods as 'best 7 of the 18 double-banana channels', not 'best possible 7'. Draw the position-cost conclusion from n=4 and n=2 only. In fig1 (x-axis = electrode count) Glass-7 sits at 8 electrodes and Best-7 near 10-14, so they are not at the same x; the caption should still flag the base and pool difference.
glass7_vs_best7.identified: Project owner, 2026-08-30, in an interactive session with Claude Code.

problem_2_quantified.measured: Re-scored every Tier A config (rf) at its locked percentile-calibrated operating points on the Tier B file subset and compared to Tier A. SzCORE: micro-sensitivity +0.003 to +0.008 absolute (mean +0.005; e.g. Full-18/LOO 0.366 -> 0.374, +2.2% relative, matching the 4/181 denominator drop). micro-FA/day -4.3% to +3.1% (mean +1.7%; sign depends on whether the dropped files carried more false positives or more recorded hours). Per-subject pass rate (the locked primary metric): unchanged for every config and criterion (delta 0.0 pp). Ali rule: micro-sensitivity shift <=+0.003, pass rate delta 0.0 pp. Conclusion: the Tier A->B base change flatters Glass-7 on the continuous metrics by well under one sensitivity point and a few percent FA, and not at all on the pass/fail conclusion.
